ops.title: WorkshopUpload code style
ops.description: WorkshopUpload (the legacy Steam Workshop publisher): tabs, Allman braces, .NET 8 with Steamworks.NET, one Program.cs, comment and control-flow rules
ops.body:
WorkshopUpload is one C# file, `tools/WorkshopUpload/Program.cs`, plus its project file, `steam_appid.txt` and Valve's `steam_api64.dll`. These are the conventions that file follows.

## Formatting

### Indentation
- Tabs, one per level, in `Program.cs`.
- `WorkshopUpload.csproj` uses two spaces.
- No `.editorconfig` or formatter is configured. TODO(owner): record the tab and brace rules in an `.editorconfig` if editors should enforce them.

### Line Length
- No limit. Usage strings and `Console.WriteLine` calls stay on one line; a long call breaks after an argument and the continuation indents one tab (the `PublishWorkshopFile` call in `Publish`).

### Braces
- Opening brace on its own line (Allman) for types, methods and multi-line blocks.
- A body of one short statement goes on the next line without braces (`if (cloudZip != null)` lines in `Update`).

## Language and Toolchain

- .NET 8 (`net8.0`), `RuntimeIdentifier` win-x64, `SelfContained` false, `Nullable` disabled, `ImplicitUsings` enabled. `LangVersion` is not set, so the .NET 8 default (C# 12) applies; the file uses file-scoped `namespace WorkshopUpload;`, switch expressions and `using var`. It runs on .NET 8, not the game's .NET Framework 4.8, so it does not import `common/oni-mod.props`.
- Steamworks.NET 2024.8.0 from NuGet is the only package. The native `steam_api64.dll` next to it (Steamworks SDK 1.60 or newer, copied to the output) is Valve's; the game's own copy is too old for this wrapper.
- `steam_appid.txt` (content `636750`) is copied to the output and must stay next to the exe.
- Build: `dotnet build tools/WorkshopUpload -c Release`.

## Imports/Includes

- The only explicit directive is `using Steamworks;` at the top, followed by the file-scoped namespace. `System`, `System.IO`, `System.Collections.Generic` and `System.Threading` arrive through implicit usings; `System.IO.Compression.ZipFile` is written out in full where used.

## Comments

### When to Comment
- The `///` summary on `Program` is the tool's manual: every command with its arguments, the legacy-API rule, and what the uploaded zip must hold. Keep it in step with the `switch` in `Main`.
- `///` summaries on constants and helpers say why: `UploaderAppId` explains the app id choice, `UploadToCloud` explains the cloud file names.
- Record field findings with a date where they drive a rule (the 2026-10-08 note on `publish`).

### When NOT to Comment
- Do not comment obvious code or leave commented-out code.
- A `// ---- commands ----` rule separates the command methods from the helpers.

## Control Structures

- `Main` prints usage and returns 2 before touching Steam, initialises Steam, then dispatches with a `switch` on `args[0]` inside `try`/`finally`.
- Each command is a `private static int` method returning its exit code; early `return 1` or `return 2` on the first failed step.
- `switch` expressions map option strings to enums (`ParseVisibility`).
- Output uses string interpolation (`$"..."`).

## Related

- See also: [error handling](error-handling.md), [naming conventions](naming-conventions.md)

ops.title: WorkshopUpload error handling
ops.description: WorkshopUpload (the legacy Steam Workshop publisher): exit codes 0/1/2, Steam result checks, Await timeouts, Check and UploadToCloud throws, and the legacy-API-only rule
ops.body:
WorkshopUpload is a console tool run by a person or by `tools/Release/release.py`. Its error handling is its exit code and what it prints. A failed Steam call must stop the run: a half-applied Workshop update is worse than none.

## Principles

1. **Check every Steam result.** Each call-result is awaited and its `EResult` compared with `k_EResultOK`; anything else prints the result and returns 1.
2. **Fail before touching Steam when the input is wrong.** Usage errors return 2 without initialising Steam.
3. **Always shut Steam down.** `SteamAPI.Shutdown()` is in a `finally` around the dispatch.
4. **Say what the user needs to do.** Messages name the likely cause (Steam not running, cloud quota, legal agreement).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Where |
|------|---------|-------|
| 0 | the command succeeded | each command method |
| 1 | `SteamAPI.Init` failed, a Steam result was not OK, or the item is not downloadable/installed | `Main`, `Info`, `Update`, `Publish`, `Download` |
| 2 | usage error: no command, unknown command, missing arguments, `--title` missing on publish | `Main`, `Update`, `Publish` |

Usage text and failures go to standard error (`Console.Error`); progress and results go to standard output.

## Handling Patterns

### Steam initialisation
```csharp
if (!SteamAPI.Init())
{
	Console.Error.WriteLine("SteamAPI.Init failed. Is the Steam client running and logged in? Is steam_appid.txt next to the exe?");
	return 1;
}
```

### Steam call results
`Await<T>` pumps `SteamAPI.RunCallbacks()` every 50 ms until the result arrives. It throws `TimeoutException` after 120 s and `Exception("Steam call I/O failure: ...")` when Steam reports an I/O failure.

### Update calls
`Check(bool ok, string what)` throws `Exception(what + " returned false")` when an `UpdatePublishedFile*` call refuses its input. `UploadToCloud` throws when `FileWrite` fails (cloud quota, or Steam Cloud disabled for the app). A failed `FileShare` only prints a warning, and the result of the later publish decides.

### Warnings that do not stop the run
`publish` without `--tags` prints a warning, because untagged items do not show up in the Workshop's browse views.

### Exceptions
There is no `catch` in the tool. A thrown exception ends the process with the .NET unhandled-exception output and a non-zero code, after `finally` has shut Steam down. `info`, `description` and `download` read `args[1]` without a length check, so a missing id ends that way rather than with a usage line. TODO(owner): add argument checks to those three commands so they return 2 with a usage line.

## Rules the code enforces

- Publishing and updating use only the legacy `ISteamRemoteStorage` API. An item touched through `ISteamUGC` item update stops being downloadable by the game, permanently. `SteamUGC` appears only in `Download`, which reads and downloads and never writes.
- `Info` reports `NOT a legacy single-file item` for an item whose `m_hFile` is invalid: the game cannot download it. `Download` reports a directory install path as a failure ("Steam failed to download the mod").

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid

- Ignoring an `EResult` and printing success.
- Adding a modern `ISteamUGC` update path for publish or update.
- Printing secrets: the tool prints the Steam persona name and id and item ids only; nothing else from the account.

## Related

- See also: [code style](code-style.md), [entities](../domains/entities.md)

ops.title: WorkshopUpload naming conventions
ops.description: WorkshopUpload (the legacy Steam Workshop publisher): command, option, method, constant and Steam Cloud file naming
ops.body:
## Files and Directories

- Folder, project file and root namespace share one name: `WorkshopUpload` (`WorkshopUpload.csproj`, `namespace WorkshopUpload;`).
- One source file, `Program.cs`. Steam files keep Valve's names: `steam_appid.txt`, `steam_api64.dll`.

## Code Naming

### Methods
- PascalCase. A command is a method named for it with an initial capital: `info` is `Info`, `description` is `Description`, `list` is `List`, `update` is `Update`, `publish` is `Publish`, `cloud` is `Cloud`, `download` is `Download`. Each takes the parsed arguments (`ulong id`, or `string[] args`) and returns the exit code.
- Helpers are verbs: `UploadToCloud`, `ParseTags`, `ParseVisibility`, `ParseOptions`, `Check`, `Await<T>`.
- All methods are `private static`; the class is `internal static class Program`.

### Constants
- PascalCase `private const`: `AppId` (457140, the game) and `UploaderAppId` (636750, Klei's uploader tool).

### Variables
- camelCase: `cloudZip`, `cloudPreview`, `zipPath`, `previewPath`, `descFile`, `tagList`.
- Option values are looked up in a `Dictionary<string, string>` called `opts`.
- Steam handle and result types keep Steamworks naming, including its Hungarian-style fields (`details.m_rgchTitle`, `page.m_nResultsReturned`, `result.m_eResult`).
- Item ids are `ulong id` and wrapped as `new PublishedFileId_t(id)`.

## Project-Specific Conventions

### Command line
- A command is the first argument, lower-case: `info`, `description`, `list`, `update`, `publish`, `cloud`, `download`.
- Options are `--kebab-case` pairs of name and value: `--title`, `--description-file`, `--changenote`, `--visibility`, `--tags`. `ParseOptions` stores them under the name without the dashes, so an option the code reads is spelled exactly as it is typed.
- Visibility words: `public`, `friends`, `unlisted`, `private` (anything else is private).
- Tags are one comma-separated string using the Workshop's own tag names (`tweaks`, `Base Game`, `Spaced Out!`).

### Steam Cloud names
- The zip is always `mod_publish_data_file.zip` and a preview is `mod_publish_preview` plus the preview's lower-cased extension. These are the names Klei's own uploader uses; the extension lets Steam treat a GIF as animated.

### Output
- `label:  value` lines padded to align (`result:   `, `title:    `, `file:     `) in `Info`; `Description`, `Cloud` and `Download` use their own short labels.

## Related

- See also: [code style](code-style.md), [glossary](../domains/glossary.md)

ops.title: WorkshopUpload domain
ops.description: WorkshopUpload (the legacy Steam Workshop publisher): the seven commands, helpers, app ids, files read and written, rules and code paths
ops.body:
## Overview

WorkshopUpload publishes and updates Oxygen Not Included mods on the Steam Workshop and inspects items. It is a .NET 8 console app over Steamworks.NET. It uses the legacy `ISteamRemoteStorage` API, which is the only kind of item the game can download. It runs as Klei's "Oxygen Not Included Uploader" tool (app 636750) with the game (app 457140) as the consumer app, and needs the Steam client running and logged in as the item's owner.

Source: `tools/WorkshopUpload/Program.cs`. `tools/Release/release.py` calls it to push a release zip, preview, description and change note to the mod's Workshop item. The commands are documented in `common/README.md`.

## Key Entities

### Program.Main
**Description**: Entry point. Prints usage (return 2) when there are no arguments, calls `SteamAPI.Init`, prints the running app id and Steam user, dispatches on `args[0]` and shuts Steam down in `finally`.
**Location**: `tools/WorkshopUpload/Program.cs`

### Commands

| Command | Method | What it does |
|---------|--------|--------------|
| `info <id>` | `Info` | prints result, title, a 90-character description excerpt, file name and size, preview handle, visibility, type, update time, and whether the item is a legacy single-file item |
| `description <id> [out.txt]` | `Description` | writes the item's live description to a file or prints it |
| `list` | `List` | pages through `EnumerateUserPublishedFiles` and prints id, title, visibility and `legacy` or `NON-LEGACY (broken)` per item |
| `update <id> [zip [preview]] [options]` | `Update` | uploads the files to Steam Cloud, builds an update request (file, preview, title, description, change note, visibility, tags, each only when given), commits it, then runs `Info` |
| `publish <zip> <preview> --title T [options]` | `Publish` | uploads zip and preview, calls `PublishWorkshopFile` as a community item (default visibility private), prints the new id and URL, then runs `Info` |
| `cloud` | `Cloud` | Steam Cloud diagnostics: enabled for account and app, quota, every cloud file with its size and persisted flag |
| `download <id>` | `Download` | has this client download the item, then reports the install path, whether it is a file (a zip, listing its entries) or a directory (a failure), and the update time |

**Location**: `Program.cs`. **Relationships**: `Update` and `Publish` call `UploadToCloud` and `ParseOptions`, and end by calling `Info`; `Info`, `Description`, `List` and `Publish` use `Await<T>`.

### Helpers
- `UploadToCloud(localPath)`: `SteamRemoteStorage.FileWrite` into the app's cloud under a fixed name, then `FileShare` to give it a UGC handle; returns the cloud name.
- `Await<T>(call, timeoutSeconds = 120)`: pumps callbacks until a call result arrives.
- `ParseOptions(args)`, `ParseTags`, `ParseVisibility`, `Check`: option, tag and visibility parsing and the Steam `bool` check.

### Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|------|-------|---------|
| `AppId` | 457140 | the game; consumer app of every item |
| `UploaderAppId` | 636750 | Klei's uploader tool; the creator app of every working item; selected by `steam_appid.txt` |

## Files read and written

| File | Direction | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `steam_appid.txt` | read by Steam | `636750`, next to the exe |
| `steam_api64.dll` | loaded | Valve's native library |
| mod zip, preview, `--description-file` | read | uploaded to Steam Cloud and the Workshop |
| `description` output file | written | the live description text |
| Steam Cloud: `mod_publish_data_file.zip`, `mod_publish_preview.<ext>` | written | staging copies shared before publish or update |
| Workshop item | written | created or changed by `publish` and `update` |

## Business Rules

- Publish and update only through `ISteamRemoteStorage`. An item updated through `ISteamUGC` stops being downloadable by the game, permanently.
- The process must run as app 636750; sharing cloud files under the game's own app id fails with FileNotFound. `steam_appid.txt` stays `636750`.
- `download` answers about the game's view of the item only when run with the environment variables `SteamAppId=457140` and `SteamGameId=457140` (ModTest sets them); otherwise it answers for the uploader app.
- The zip holds `mod.yaml`, `mod_info.yaml`, the DLL and `preview.png` at its root, as Klei's uploader produces.
- Prefer Klei's uploader for new items: the one item `publish` created (2026-10-08) never appeared in the Workshop's Most Recent listing. Updating existing items with this tool is proven.
- Give `publish` a category tag plus the DLCs supported, since the Workshop's browse views key off tags.
- Read the live description (`description`) before overwriting it, since it can be edited on the Workshop page.

## Key Code Paths

- **Update an item**: `Main` -> `Update` -> `UploadToCloud` (zip, preview) -> `CreatePublishedFileUpdateRequest` -> `UpdatePublishedFile*` through `Check` -> `CommitPublishedFileUpdate` -> `Info` -- `Program.cs`.
- **Publish an item**: `Main` -> `Publish` -> `UploadToCloud` x2 -> `PublishWorkshopFile` -> `Info`.
- **Release use**: `tools/Release/release.py` runs `update` with the release zip, the preview, the tags, the description file and the change note, `description` to read the live text first, and `list` to find an item id by title.

TODO(owner): `common/README.md` lists a `ugc-describe` command that `Main` does not dispatch, and the usage line printed by `Main` omits `description` and `cloud`; decide whether to add `ugc-describe` or drop it from the README, and bring the usage text in line.

## State Transitions

None kept by the tool. The Workshop item carries visibility (`private`, `friends`, `unlisted`, `public`) that `publish` sets at creation and `update --visibility` changes.

## Related

- See also: [glossary](glossary.md)
- Governed by: [naming conventions](../standards/naming-conventions.md)

ops.title: WorkshopUpload glossary
ops.description: WorkshopUpload (the legacy Steam Workshop publisher): terms a newcomer needs: legacy item, uploader app, consumer app, Steam Cloud staging, tags, visibility
ops.body:
Terms a newcomer to WorkshopUpload needs. The tool's own things are in [entities](entities.md).

## Abbreviations and Acronyms

| Abbreviation | Full Term | Context |
|--------------|-----------|---------|
| UGC | user-generated content | Steam's name for Workshop files; a UGC handle is what a shared cloud file gets |
| ONI | Oxygen Not Included | the game, app 457140 |
| DLC | downloadable content | Workshop tags name the DLCs an item supports |
| EResult | Steam's result code | `k_EResultOK` is success; checked after every call |

## Terms to Avoid

| Avoid | Use Instead | Reason |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| "upload" for a Workshop item change | update, or publish for a new item | the commands are `update` and `publish`; "upload" is the Steam Cloud write (`UploadToCloud`) |
| steamcmd or `workshop_build_item` for ONI items | this tool or Klei's uploader | steamcmd items are manifest-based and fail to download for every subscriber |
| ISteamUGC for publishing | ISteamRemoteStorage | an item touched through `ISteamUGC` item update stops being downloadable by the game, permanently |

## Cross-Domain Terms

### Legacy item
**Definition**: A Workshop item made through `ISteamRemoteStorage`: one zip file that Steam installs as `<handle>_legacy.bin` and the game opens with `ZipFile`. ONI has no Workshop depot, so only legacy items download.
**Used in**: `Info` (`Legacy single-file item` or `NOT a legacy single-file item`), `List`, `Download`.

### Uploader app (636750)
**Definition**: Klei's "Oxygen Not Included Uploader" tool, free with the game. The tool runs as this app, set by `steam_appid.txt`, because cloud files shared under the game's own id fail with FileNotFound. It is the `creator_app_id` of every working item.
**Used in**: `UploaderAppId`, `Main`.

### Consumer app (457140)
**Definition**: The game; the app whose Workshop the item belongs to and whose players download it.
**Used in**: `AppId`, `PublishWorkshopFile`.

### Steam Cloud staging
**Definition**: The step where the zip and preview are written into the user's Steam Cloud for the uploader app under fixed names and shared, so the publish or update call can refer to them.
**Used in**: `UploadToCloud`.

### Tags
**Definition**: Workshop labels that its browse views filter on: a category (`tweaks`) plus supported DLCs (`Base Game`, `Spaced Out!`, `The Frosty Planet Pack`, `The Bionic Booster Pack`, `The Prehistoric Planet Pack`, `The Aquatic Planet Pack`).
**Used in**: `--tags`, `ParseTags`.

### Visibility
**Definition**: `public`, `friends`, `unlisted` or `private`. `publish` defaults to private.
**Used in**: `ParseVisibility`, `--visibility`.

### Change note
**Definition**: The text shown in an item's change history, set with `update --changenote`.
**Used in**: `Update`, `release.py`.

## Related

- See also: [entities](entities.md)
